q: Walk me through normalising an F-Log2 clip with four nodes.
a: 1. Check the clip is read as F-Log2 (Interpret Footage) and the sequence works in DaVinci Wide Gamut (Sequence ▸ Color Management). 2. Add Node, then + Serial three times: nodes 01–04 (name them Balance, Exposure, Contrast, Saturation with `grade.labelNode` if you like). 3. Node 01: Temperature, Tint and Offset until something white or grey looks neutral. 4. Node 02: Gain for the brightest important part, then Gamma for faces. 5. Node 03: Contrast a little at a time, Pivot at 0.336 unless faces get too dark. 6. Node 04: Saturation until colours look natural. 7. Bypass twice to compare. Grab a still to reuse the tree.

q: In Premiere I'd use Lumetri with an input LUT on log. How do I do that in Revolution?
a: Let colour management do the conversion (Interpret Footage as F-Log2, a DaVinci Wide Gamut sequence), then grade with a few fixed nodes: Balance, Exposure, Contrast, Saturation. Lumetri still works afterwards if you want it.

q: Why warm only the highlights and mids?
a: Warming the highlights and mids while keeping the shadows neutral looks natural; warming everything looks like a filter. On a node after your technical nodes: drag the Gain puck a short way towards orange, the Gamma puck even less; if the shadows look muddy, nudge Lift slightly towards blue. Toggle the node to judge, and reduce it there if too strong. Quicker but blunter: raise Temperature on that node.

q: Why should the shadows stay neutral when I cool a shot?
a: Light moving towards blue reads as cooler, and it looks natural when the light turns blue but skin and whites stay believable. On a new node: Gain puck a short way to blue, Gamma less, Lift near the centre (or slightly orange if the shadows turn heavy blue). Check a face: grey or purple skin means too strong. Lowering Temperature is quicker but cools everything evenly, more like a filter.

q: How do I get a sunset shot to read as blue?
a: Tungsten light is far more orange than daylight, so gentle moves to blue only pull it back towards neutral. Neutralise first: WB picker (or Auto) on something that should be white or grey. Then cool: Offset towards blue, then Gain further for the light itself (go further than feels safe, then back off), or Temperature well below 0. Check the vectorscope cloud sits towards blue; protect skin with a qualifier node if it goes grey or purple.

q: What if faces show grey in the sky matte?
a: On a node at the end: Qualifier tab ▸ Pick the sky, Add a lighter and darker part. View ▸ Matte: the sky white, faces black; if a face shows grey, narrow Hue width; if the sky is speckled, raise Qualifier softness or Matte blur. Back to Normal, then in Primaries raise Saturation a little and drag the Gain puck slightly to blue. If blue clothing or water changed too, add a Linear window over the top of the frame.

q: How do I make a bedside lamp glow green?
a: On a node at the end: add a Circle window over the lamp and its glow with a lot of Softness so the change fades with distance; optionally a qualifier on the glow (Pick, Add, check the Matte, raise softness) so the node acts only where both agree. In Primaries drag Gain well towards the new colour (add Offset for a very orange light) until the glow reads that colour. Leave the bulb's core a little lighter. Toggle the node to check the far walls are unchanged; track the window if the camera moves.

q: How do I draw the eye to a face?
a: Viewers look at faces first, so lifting a face a little without touching the background draws the eye. On a node at the end: Windows ▸ Circle, a bit larger than the face, Softness up until the edge can't be seen, then raise the Gamma ring slightly. Track the window if the person moves.

a: Viewers look at faces first, so lifting a face a little without touching the background draws the eye. On a node at the end: Windows ▸ Circle, a bit larger than the face, Softness up until the edge can't be seen, then raise the Gamma ring slightly. Track the window if the person moves.

q: Which shot do I grade first when matching angles?
a: Grade the shot you like best (usually the wide) first and Grab Still. On the close-up click the still for a wipe and line the divider up on something both share (a face, else a wall or sky). Open the Match tab, choose the wide as Reference, Shot Match; fine-tune the new node (levels, then Temperature), then Compare shots to read what still differs. Off leaves the comparison.

q: How do I use a still and Shot Match together?
a: Grade the shot you like best (usually the wide) first and Grab Still. On the close-up click the still for a wipe and line the divider up on something both share (a face, else a wall or sky). Open the Match tab, choose the wide as Reference, Shot Match; fine-tune the new node (levels, then Temperature), then Compare shots to read what still differs. Off leaves the comparison.

q: When can clips share one grade?
a: Clips shot in the same place and light can share one grade. Copy Grade on the one you like, select the others, Paste Grade (or Append Grade to keep their own nodes). Then Check scene in the Match tab names the clip that stands out most: fix that one by hand.

q: How do I make clips from different cameras feel like one film?
a: A little grain hides banding and makes clips from different sources feel like one film. Add it on the last node so nothing after it sharpens or blurs it: raise Grain strength until you can just see it at full size, then back off; Grain size for coarser, Grain softness for smoother. Use the same three numbers on the other clips.

q: How much saturation should I add to skin?
a: After a log normalisation or under green-ish or overcast light, faces can look grey while the rest is fine. After the overall balance, add a Skin node: Pick the cheek or forehead, Add lighter and darker parts, check the Matte (narrow Hue width against wood or orange clothes, raise softness), back to Normal. Raise Saturation only a few steps (skin turns orange quickly) and Temperature slightly; Gamma a touch if dull. Toggle the node: healthier, not obviously different.

q: and if the matte flickers when they move?
a: Set View to Matte while the clip plays; if it flickers on the moving face, raise Qualifier softness (and Matte blur if speckled), then go back to Normal.
